title: Lord, We Are Blind, We Mortals Blind
description: Lord, We Are Blind, We Mortals Blind in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 26, headed “God invisible”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, we are blind, we mor-tals blind, We can't be-hold thy bright a-bode; O 'tis be-yond a crea-ture mind To glance a thought half way to God.

lines: Lord, we are blind, we mortals blind,
We can't behold thy bright abode;
To glance a thought half-way to God.
Where neither wings nor soul can fly,
Nor angels climb the topless throne.
The Lord of glory builds his seat
And lays beneath his sacred feet
Yet, glorious Lord, thy gracious eyes
Look thro', and cheer us from above;
Beyond our praise thy grandeur flies,
Yet we adore, and yet we love.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
